what_it_is: The briefing discipline: mint at the last responsible moment from live bytes; open with how to think (why it matters in plain words, core principles for THIS task, a pre-mortem naming the closest past failures, the Q2 scenario, the coach's note); carry exactly one verifiable outcome sized to one session with exclusions named; state authority explicitly (what she decides, where she must stop); stamp freshness in (re-pin at action time — the brief admits its own half-life); paste the 3 latest broadcasts verbatim, never summarized.
what_it_does: Gives the worker everything she needs to win cold. A Naya who wakes into the brief should never have to go hunting. If a cold Naya reads only a brief and does the work wrong, the brief failed first — fix the brief, teach the fix, add the gate. Diagnostic, never punitive.
why_it_matters: The model brief (brief-t0793-lane3.md, minted 2026-10-14): opens with Why this matters ('Two decision authorities is a governance hole, not a backup'), core principles for THIS task, a PRE-MORTEM naming the two closest analog failures, a Q2-scenario and the COACH'S NOTE — thinking before doing. Single verifiable outcome with a numbered definition of done naming exact artifacts. Authority explicit: 'Read-only repo analysis. Any step that would alter production behavior or authority: stop, file DECISION REQUIRED.' Freshness stamped: 're-pin the tip via git ls-remote at action time and do all work at that pin… derive it from live bytes, never from memory or this brief.' The opposite: the Wave-108 stale-assignment failure — a validation brief dispatched 6.3 hours after the work it asked for was DELIVERED; triage read the header, the truth was in the tail. And the re-brief on a false premise: a re-issue brief claimed the earlier brief 'went stale (claimed, no receipt, 8 ticks)' while the receipt existed at twelve-lane-receipts/t0537-lane9.md and the branch was live on origin — the worker refused to rebuild and named the repair: the dispatcher's 'stale' metadata must cite receipt-directory evidence or it's a claim without proof.
key_rules: A brief is a hypothesis minted at spawn time from live state, scoped to one verifiable outcome inside one 30–45-minute session, opening with how to think.
If an unbriefed Naya can't succeed from the brief alone, the brief failed — never the worker.
Open with thinking (why it matters → core principles for THIS task → pre-mortem → scenario → coach's note) before what to do.
Exactly one verifiable outcome, sized to one session, with exclusions named and exact artifacts in the definition of done.
Authority explicit in one sentence each: what she decides, and where she must stop (DECISION REQUIRED).
Freshness stamped in: re-pin at action time. The brief admits its own half-life — derive from live bytes, never from memory or the brief.
Paste the 3 latest broadcasts verbatim — never summarized or paraphrased.
A re-brief's 'stale' claim must cite receipt-directory evidence, or it's a claim without proof.
Delivery, not destination: the brief comes to her; she never goes hunting for docs.
test: Could a Naya who has read nothing else succeed from this brief alone — world, thinking, outcome, bounds, proof — without going hunting?
Was it generated at spawn time from live bytes — and does it say which bytes, with a freshness stamp or a re-pin instruction?
Does it carry exactly one verifiable outcome, sized to one 30–45-minute session — with the exclusions named?
Does the definition of done name exact artifacts (paths, fields, SHAs), not vibes?
Does the worker know what she decides and where she must stop (DECISION REQUIRED), in one sentence each?
Does it open with how to think (why it matters, core principles for THIS task, pre-mortem, scenario) before what to do?
Is the premise re-derived, not inherited — would the brief's own facts survive a live-bytes check right now?
Are the 3 latest broadcasts pasted verbatim — never summarized or paraphrased?
If it's a re-brief, does it cite the staleness evidence — or is 'stale' an unproven claim?

enforcement.real: The brief lifecycle on disk: brief-queue/ (unclaimed) → claimed/ → done/ / stale/ / superseded/. The claim-liveness audit every tick. receipt_checker.py — the board post isn't done until it passes. The contract gate's sign-in/sign-out. violation-detector-class17.py. The template's sign-in block on the lane feed BEFORE any read. bin/verify-brief-pins.py — write-time SHA pin verification. The dispatcher mints briefs per tick from the living plan with the current machine shape.
enforcement.proposed: A machine brief-completeness lint at mint time — pin verification exists, but no script today checks that a brief carries a freshness stamp, a single verifiable outcome, and a pre-mortem before it enters the queue. Enforcement of the shape is dispatcher discipline + worker feedback + the Balancer's eye. Named honestly as the gap.
